# Welcome Pack Payment Leaflet

Fictional evaluation document. Scope: fees administration for the 2027 policy year. Effective dates are supplied separately in the corpus manifest. This document must be read alongside other selected sources when the question names another office or location.

## Registration charge

The welcome pack leaflet sets the annual registration charge at AUD 52 per student.

A printed amount is evidence of what that document says, not permission to silently override another active schedule. Staff preserve both sources when referring a discrepancy. Discount percentages and due dates are separate questions. For this section the desk records the request under FEES-2027-01. The reference groups correspondence; it does not change the deadline or amount stated above. A correction must preserve the original entry and record the reason for the change.

## Working example: registration charge

Consider a case where a household compares a welcome leaflet with an account statement. The immediate question concerns registration charge, not every rule in the fees file. The administrator checks billing contacts, instalment references, and receipts before replying. A common error is that a registration line is mistaken for a tuition instalment. Read the named source and policy year before treating a nearby number as the answer. Record which document supported the explanation so that another staff member can reproduce the check. If the request also mentions a different service, preserve it as a separate issue instead of assuming that one approval covers both activities.

## Cross-service boundary

This fees document does not grant authority over unrelated activities. A staff member should distinguish the stated rule from a future booking, payment, or discretionary approval. A family may ask several questions in one message; answerable portions should cite the relevant source while missing facts remain unresolved. An unanswered detail must not be inferred from an adjacent fee, deadline, room number, or event identifier. In particular, general guidance about billing contacts, instalment references, and receipts is not a substitute for an explicit rule about a different programme.

## Handling incomplete requests

When a fees request omits the student, location, policy year, or relevant date, the desk records the missing information and asks for it. The original wording is preserved in the working notes. Staff avoid copying identity documents into teaching chat or broad distribution lists. A later clarification supplements rather than overwrites the request. This distinction matters when a household compares a welcome leaflet with an account statement. A response acknowledging receipt is administrative correspondence and should not be represented as approval of an exception.

## Audit example and non-equivalence

The reviewer reconstructs the event from billing contacts, instalment references, and receipts. For example, an entered reference code may identify correspondence without proving that money moved, a class place was reserved, or a consent decision changed. The reviewer compares the dated source with the actual record and records unresolved inconsistencies. Similar words across offices are not proof of identical policies: deposit, credit, submission, and acknowledgement each have a specific role in their own service. The desk retains source identity rather than combining conflicting numbers into a new undocumented rule.

## Final receipt delivery

The welcome pack requires electronic receipts to be sent to the nominated billing contact rather than every household contact.

This is the last substantive instruction in this source. The closing check must be performed after the ordinary service tasks, not inferred from an earlier example. Preserve a short completion note with the responsible staff role and source reference. If the closing check cannot be verified, mark the item unresolved rather than copying a previous day’s completion status. End of policy text.
